summary:
La Rioja is an autonomous community of Spain and stands under the national legal framework, which applies across its territory.

The community passed its own trans-rights law in February 2022, recorded in a national trans federation report dated 18 February 2022, which places La Rioja among the autonomous communities where trans people may self-declare their legal gender. The regional law has applied to trans residents and visitors since 2022 and remains in force alongside the national trans statute of 28 February 2023.

La Rioja is listed among the communities that prohibit conversion therapies.

The community created a regional registry for same-sex couples in 2010.
tangentialFactors:
The regional law operates alongside the national framework rather than replacing it, and both remain in force.

La Rioja's 2022 statute was adopted roughly a year before the national trans statute and has not been repealed, so the community's self-declaration route and conversion-therapy ban operate in addition to the national regime.
localsOnly:
People living in La Rioja can use the community's 2022 law to self-declare their legal gender and are covered by its prohibition on conversion therapies; the law has applied to residents since 2022.

The 2010 registry for same-sex couples is a community-level instrument open to residents of La Rioja.
outOfScopeNotes:
The regional law is documented through a secondary citation: a national trans federation report of 18 February 2022 reproduced on a public reference page. The law's official number, gazette publication and full text are not sourced.

No La Rioja-specific enforcement record was identified. The sources contain no regional prosecutions, hate-crime statistics or incidents involving trans people in the community.

Whether the regional self-declaration route imposes steps or offers benefits beyond the national route is unresolved in the sources.

Region-specific information on facility access, policing practice and trans healthcare provision in La Rioja is not sourced.
